title: introduce-sealed-audit-envelope-v3-and-kms-custody-validator
author: Priya Nandakumar
description:
Motivation: Customers in regulated geographies asked for stronger non-repudiable audit envelopes plus an operator-facing custody validation step that ties audit writes to a jurisdiction-bound KMS proof. This PR implements a sealed-audit-envelope v3 format, a KMS custody validator middleware that verifies provider-signed custody assertions at write-time, and an RBAC v2 policy hook to soft-enforce region-pin decisions during rollout.

What this PR introduces (high-level):
- sealed-audit-envelope v3: canonical JSON envelope with compact Merkle summary, HMAC-lite for fast verification, and an optional KMS-custody-assertion field. Backwards compatible: readers fall back to v2 when v3 flag absent.
- kms-custody-validator: middleware used by audit-proxy and private-installer that validates a custody assertion from allowed KMS providers (aws-kms, gcp-kms, onprem-hsm). Validator supports multi-provider key proof (primary signature + optional witness signature).
- region-pin decision hook: an RBAC v2 policy adapter that can reject audit writes if the tenant's claimed geozone doesn't match the KMS origin. The hook is soft-rolled: by default it emits an audit violation metric and warning but allows writes for 30 days; rollout controlled via feature-flagging.
- CLI/installer flags: private-installer gains --enforce-kms-custody and --audit-envelope-version with migration helpers.
- diagnostics & tooling: new CLI tool auditctl validate-envelope and a lightweight kubernetes admission test for installer smoke runs.

Design notes:
- Custody assertion format is provider-agnostic: {provider, key_alias, signed_token, signature_algo}. Tokens are short-lived (1m) and include a provenance claim (region, account-id, timestamp). Validator performs: token signature check with provider root, timestamp freshness, and optional witness verify when configured.
- To avoid writer perf regressions, validator uses a local soft-cache of validated custody tokens keyed by signature thumbprint with TTL (default 30s). Sharded validation workers perform cryptographic checks asynchronously for large fanout requests; on fast-path we validate synchronously when envelope includes witness signature.
- Rollout path: feature-flag disabled -> metric-only -> warning (soft-fail) -> hard enforce. All stages emit telemetry for false positives so SRE/Compliance can tune allowlists.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor (review): Can we avoid an extra network hop on the fast-path by validating only the token thumbprint synchronously? I worry about latency impact on high-throughput audit writers.
Priya Nandakumar (reply): Agreed - implemented a thumbprint cache (30s default). Large fanout requests fall back to async shard validators; updated design notes explaining tradeoffs.
Sofia Martinez (review): The policy hook needs a clear allowlist override for cross-account migrations. Also request a small migration tool to backfill custody assertions for consoles that upgrade.
Priya Nandakumar (reply): Added allowlist config + migration helper in installer. Documented backfill steps in docs/rollouts.
Ethan Brooks (security): Add unit tests that simulate a forged witness signature and ensure we emit an audit alert and (when feature flag is on) reject write.
Priya Nandakumar (reply): Added tests and an integration case using the HSM emulator. CI matrix now runs the onprem path in a separate job.

release_notes: Added sealed audit envelope v3 with optional KMS custody assertions, a KMS custody validator for audit writes, RBAC v2 region-pin soft-enforcement hook, and installer flags to control rollout. Backwards compatible readers supported. Ops: follow docs/rollouts/audit-custody-rollout.md for staged enforcement.
